liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Mighty Quinn (Quinn The Eskimo)** (2 reviews): Truckin' and Mighty Quinn were the only songs the reviewer remembers; Reviewer had heard rumors of a cover on that tour and correctly predicted Mighty Quinn would appear [10][12]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Bobby's Little Red Rooster is one of only three performances that spring; Brent's Hammond solo rescues it, while the slide solo screeches [9]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Jerry sounds hoarse, so the Friend Of The Devil is less than gorgeous [9]
- **Desolation Row** (1 review): Reviewer highlights Bobby's Desolation Row as part of a night where everything clicked [12]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Eyes is rushed but played with refreshing inventiveness [17]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer finds this the most boring Drums they've ever heard, and the rest of second set part two weaker [17]

## Setlist highlights

- **Bill Graham Announcement's**: back after 295 archived shows (1651 days); rare: 4 archived performances [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-04-17.141128.sbd.miller.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 150 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Mix changes occur during Cold Rain And Snow [1]
- **gd1987-04-17.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83731.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 3.2/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1987-04-17.senn441.corso.86837.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 2/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd87-04-17.sbd.clugston.11872.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 143 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [7]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds fantastic: crisp highs, clear bass, no honky mids, with Bobby slightly left, Brent slightly right, Jerry centered [15]

## Around the show

- Reviewer wryly notes the song title Cold Rain And Snow is odd for rarely cold, nearly precipitation-free Southern California [9]
- Reviewer's first show, attended while tripping, standing at the top of the amphitheater and watching the lights of Irvine [10]
- Reviewer lived in Southern California, mail-ordered tickets right away, and enjoyed a pre-show party [12]
- A chipwich vendor came around just as the show started [16]
- Reviewer attended as a Pitzer College freshman with roommate Joe Pass Jr., recalling the show as rainy and cold [18]
- Performance is called a solid, sometimes very hot, example of 1987 Dead [15]
- By spring 1987 standards, reviewer considers this show a real sucker [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-04-17.141128.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [1]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to make the show complete [1]
- **gd1987-04-17.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83731.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Maxell MX90/Sony D5) [2]. Also: Schoeps CMC3/MK4 mics to PCM, DAT and CD; tapes labeled Broadcast Mix, from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [2]
- **gd1987-04-17.senn441.corso.86837.sbeok.flac16**: taped by John Corso; transferred by Alex Ford; source: Sennheiser 441s > D5 > D5 > gold plated Monster Cables > D5 > Maxell XLII-S 90 (set I) TDK MA-R90 (set II) [4]. Also: Master audience cassettes from Mark McCue; Alex Ford transferred, edited and seeded in August 2007, patching tape flips [4]
- **gd87-04-17.sbd.clugston.11872.sbeok.shnf**: source: Master Soundboard Casette > PCM> DAT> CDREAC'ed/SHN'ed & seeded to etree by Scott Clugston [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1987-04-17 Irvine Meadows, Irvine, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-04-17-irvine-meadows-irvine-ca-usa/) [22]
- Fan art by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1987-04-17 Fri Good Friday Irvine Meadows Amphitheatre, Irvine, CA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1361994577989/grateful-dead-1987-04-17-fri-good-friday) [23]
